definition: Edge detection includes a variety of mathematical methods that aim at identifying edges, defined as curves in a digital image at which the image brightness changes sharply or, more formally, has discontinuities.
details: The same problem of finding discontinuities in one-dimensional signals is known as step detection and the problem of finding signal discontinuities over time is known as change detection. Edge detection is a fundamental tool in image processing, machine vision and computer vision, particularly in the areas of feature detection and feature extraction.

explainer.lead: Edge detection finds curves in a digital image where brightness changes sharply. These curves give image-processing and computer-vision systems a compact way to locate and extract visual features.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a colouring book where a black shape sits on a white page: the sudden change from dark to light helps you see its outline. Edge detection looks for similar sudden changes in a picture and marks the curves where they happen. This helps computers find useful features in images.
tiers.practitioner: Apply an edge-detection method to a digital image to identify curves at sharp brightness changes or discontinuities, then use those curves for feature detection or feature extraction. Do not treat edge detection as one fixed algorithm: it covers a variety of mathematical methods. Keep the related problems distinct: step detection concerns one-dimensional signals, while change detection concerns signal discontinuities over time.
tiers.paperLevel: Edges are defined as curves in a digital image at which image brightness changes sharply or, more formally, has discontinuities. Edge detection denotes a family of mathematical methods for identifying those curves. Its one-dimensional analogue is step detection, while detecting signal discontinuities over time is called change detection.

explainer.example: In a grayscale image, suppose one region has brightness values near 20 and the adjacent region has values near 200. The sharp transition between them is identified as an edge, forming a curve along the boundary between the dark and bright regions.

usedIn.name: Image processing
usedIn.detail: Used as a fundamental tool for locating sharp brightness transitions in digital images.

usedIn.name: Machine vision
usedIn.detail: Supports the identification of image features from detected edges.

usedIn.name: Computer vision
usedIn.detail: Provides curves at image discontinuities for feature detection and feature extraction.

explainer.intuition: A sharp change in brightness marks a meaningful transition in an image. Edge detection turns those transitions into curves that can be used as visual features.
howItWorks: Start with a digital image containing brightness values.
Examine the image for sharp brightness changes or discontinuities.
Identify the locations where those changes occur.
Mark the resulting curves as edges for feature detection or extraction.
explainer.whyItMatters: Edge detection is a fundamental tool in image processing, machine vision and computer vision. It is especially important for feature detection and feature extraction.
misconceptions: Edge detection is not one single method; it includes a variety of mathematical methods.
An edge is defined by sharp brightness change or discontinuity, not simply by being an object's outline.
Step detection and change detection are related problems in one-dimensional signals and signals over time, respectively.
